newsitem.title: POLAND: HSBC to ready Polish PBK data by end-Jan. [CORRECTED 18:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: HSBC to ready Polish PBK data by end-Jan. [CORRECTED 18:45 GMT]

text.p: HSBC Investment Services, chosen by Poland in November to advise on the sale of Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK), should have an information memorandum on the bank ready by the end of the month, Hubert Janiszewski, the head of HSBC's Polish unit, said.
The finance ministry plans to sell 65 percent of PBK to a foreign or domestic strategic investor or to a group of investors by the end of April.
"If the ministry says it wants to sell the controlling stake by the end of April, then there would have to be at least three months for the proceedings," Janiszewski told Reuters on Monday.
He said an advertisement inviting investors to negotiate for the stake would appear in the Polish press once the memorandum was made available.
The ministry has said it would also probably offer a 15 percent stake in PBK to small investors in September, with a public-offering prospectus likely ready by late June.
PBK employees are expected to get a 15-percent stake and five percent would go for restitution claims.
PBK netted 185.17 million zlotys over the first three quarters of 1996 against 121.07 million zlotys for all of 1995.
It had a balance sheet total of 8.37 billion zlotys after three quarters against 7.37 billion (corrects from million) zlotys at the end of 1995.

Janiszewski has said several foreign and domestic investors were interested in PBK, but has declined to elaborate. Poland's Kredyt Bank and Polish Development Bank (PBR) have signalled their interest in the privatisation.
